title: A Survey on IEEE 802.11bn Wi-Fi 8: Advantages of Ultra High Reliability for Next Generation Wireless LANs

analysis_policy.exclude_scope: References, author bios/photos, acknowledgments, appendix, nomenclature
analysis_policy.notes: Abbreviation and comparison tables inside body counted as visuals; stop before references.

raw_headings: A. The Evolution of WLAN and Motivation
section_flow.objective: Motivate Wi-Fi 8 UHR, show evolution/timeline, contrast with prior Wi-Fi surveys, state contributions and paper map.
key_components: Problem framing: Wi-Fi 7 limits for reliability/latency in dense deployments
Related-survey comparison table to surface gap
notable_moves: Uses a glossary table and a survey-comparison table inside the intro to assert novelty
Employs a timeline figure and structure figure to orient readers early

evidence_locators.claim: States Wi-Fi 7 cannot meet UHR reliability/latency in dense scenarios, motivating 802.11bn.

locator.heading: A. The Evolution of WLAN and Motivation

evidence_locators.claim: Compares existing surveys and notes lack of full Wi-Fi 8/UHR coverage.
Lists contributions and provides organization roadmap with figures.

section_flow.objective: Explain UHR-oriented PHY enhancements (DRU, MCS, 2xLDPC) with signaling logic and summarize lessons.
key_components: Problem context for each feature (e.g., interference, coding gain)
Key takeaways bullet block after each feature
notable_moves: Repeats a feature-description plus Key Takeaways pattern to compress lessons
Uses tables to list PHY enhancements and reference sources

evidence_locators.claim: Introduces DRU, MCS, and 2xLDPC with reliability rationale, each ending with key takeaways.

raw_headings: B. HiP Enhanced Distributed Channel Access
section_flow.objective: Detail MAC-layer UHR features (SMD, HiP-EDCA, NPCA, DSO) and distill actionable lessons.
key_components: Problem framing per feature (mobility, contention, spectrum use)
Key Takeaways blocks after each feature
notable_moves: Mirrors PHY section pattern to maintain rhythm: mechanism then Key Takeaways
Highlights multi-AP coordination and contention handling as recurring themes

evidence_locators.claim: Covers SMD, HiP-EDCA, NPCA, and DSO with operational logic and takeaways.

key_components: Case snippets for channel access, compression, and scheduling
notable_moves: Places a CSI/efforts table upfront to anchor the AI/ML taxonomy
Ends with future directions that tie back to earlier layer-wise gaps

raw_headings: V. CURRENT CHALLENGES AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS
section_flow.objective: Summarize challenges and open issues for UHR PHY/MAC/AI features and point to research directions.
key_components: Reliability and latency hurdles per feature group
Prospective research themes linked to earlier sections
notable_moves: Challenges mirror the earlier PHY/MAC/AI structure for continuity

evidence_locators.claim: Lists challenges and future directions aligned with PHY/MAC/AI themes.

locator.heading: V. CURRENT CHALLENGES AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS

section_flow.objective: Close the survey by reiterating UHR scope and linking to future work.
notable_moves: Conclusion is brief, restating reliability focus and future needs

evidence_locators.claim: Restates UHR focus and future directions succinctly.

hook.evidence: Highlights Wi-Fi 7 throughput but notes reliability/latency shortfalls in dense deployments.

gap.evidence: States lack of comprehensive Wi-Fi 8/UHR survey covering PHY, MAC, and AI/ML.

yes_but.evidence: Existing Wi-Fi surveys focus on Wi-Fi 7 or narrow topics like MAP-Co or AI without UHR scope.

contribution.evidence: Lists contributions: deep dive into PHY/MAC enhancements, AI/ML roles, and challenges.

organization.evidence: Provides roadmap and references structure figure early.

scope_boundary.evidence: Focuses on Wi-Fi 8 (802.11bn) reliability features and AI/ML integration, excluding broader wireless topics.

rhetorical_moves_global.reader_contract_pattern: Motivate Wi-Fi 8 reliability gap; compare surveys; dive into PHY then MAC features with takeaways; add AI/ML layer taxonomy; end with challenges and concise conclusion.

branches: AI/ML applications (CSI compression, channel access, cross-layer)

visuals_tables.layout_logic: Intro packs a glossary table, survey comparison table, and timeline figure; each major technical section interleaves figures with feature explanations and ends with key-takeaway bullets; AI/ML section anchors with a CSI efforts table.

figures.purpose: orient reader to Wi-Fi evolution and motivate UHR

tables.purpose: differentiate this Wi-Fi 8 survey from prior work

lesson_blocks.lesson: Introduce each UHR PHY mechanism, then condense pros/cons in a Key Takeaways block.
Repeat the pattern for MAC features, tying reliability goals to contention and mobility control.
Layer AI/ML use cases by protocol layer and support with an efforts table before future directions.
Mirror earlier layer structure to state gaps and open research cleanly.

synthesis.aha_moment: Using repeated feature-plus-Key-Takeaways blocks across PHY and MAC builds a tutorial rhythm that keeps dense standard content navigable.

style.section_openers_pattern: Each major section opens by naming the reliability problem, then introduces the feature set and signals a Key Takeaways block.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Intro with glossary, gap table, and timeline
steps: Open with limitations of the latest generation (Wi-Fi 7) for the target objective.
Insert a glossary/abbreviation table to normalize terms early.
Use a comparison table of prior surveys to surface the unaddressed gap.
Show a timeline figure and state contributions plus paper map.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Combines urgency, shared terminology, and evidence of novelty with early navigation aids.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Feature tutorial pattern with Key Takeaways
steps: For each feature, start with the reliability problem context.
End with a Key Takeaways bullet block before moving on.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Creates a predictable rhythm that helps readers digest dense standard updates.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Layered AI/ML taxonomy anchored by a CSI table
steps: Lead with a concise table of AI/ML efforts (e.g., CSI compression).
Discuss use cases per layer (PHY, MAC, cross-layer).
Tie each use case back to reliability goals.
Close with future directions aligned to the layer taxonomy.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Grounds abstract AI/ML claims in concrete cases and keeps coverage organized by protocol layer.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Challenges that mirror earlier structure
steps: List challenges per previously covered feature group (PHY, MAC, AI/ML).
For each, restate the reliability objective and the blocker.
Offer concise future directions tied to the blocker.
Keep this section brief to maintain momentum into the conclusion.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Maintains structural continuity, helping readers connect open problems to earlier content.
